situation: In Garoua, a new mosque is built on a foundation of very hard, grey stones with small crystals, brought from a quarry near the hills. Some walls in town are built with sandstone blocks that show thin layers.
In a new office, Zara sees a shiny floor of polished stone with wavy bands. She wonders why there are so many types of rocks, and where they come from.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Zara does not know why there are different types of rocks or where they come from.
Name the three materials described in the situation.
They are hard grey stones with crystals, sandstone blocks with layers, and a polished stone with wavy bands.
Why is it useful to know the types of rocks?
It helps us to choose strong stones for building, to find useful minerals and to understand the landscape.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to classify the rocks of the crust and to understand how they are formed and changed.

qa.a: A rock is a natural, solid material of the crust, made of one or more minerals.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: A rock is a natural, solid material of the Earth's crust made of one or more minerals.

qa.q: How are igneous rocks formed? Give two examples.
qa.a: They are formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. Examples: granite, which cools slowly underground, and basalt, which cools quickly at the surface, as at Mount Cameroon.

qa.q: How are sedimentary rocks formed? Give two examples.
qa.a: They are formed when layers of sediments (sand, mud, shells) are pressed and cemented together. Examples: sandstone, found around Garoua, and limestone, found at Figuil.

qa.q: How are metamorphic rocks formed? Give two examples.
qa.a: They are formed when existing rocks are changed by great heat and pressure. Examples: marble (from limestone), slate (from shale) and gneiss (from granite).

qa.q: In which type of rock do we usually find fossils? Why?
qa.a: Fossils are found mainly in sedimentary rocks, because plants and animals were buried in the layers of sediments.

sum.title: II. Classification of Rocks According to Origin
sum.intro: According to their origin, rocks are classified into three types:
items: A. Igneous Rocks
– Formation: cooling and hardening of magma or lava.
– Characteristics: hard, made of crystals, no layers, no fossils.
– Examples: granite (Mandara Mountains), basalt (Mount Cameroon).
B. Sedimentary Rocks
– Formation: layers of sediments are pressed and cemented together.
– Characteristics: layers (strata), often softer, may contain fossils.
– Examples: sandstone (Garoua area), limestone (Figuil), clay, shale.
C. Metamorphic Rocks
– Formation: existing rocks are changed by great heat and pressure.
– Characteristics: very hard, often with bands; minerals are rearranged.
– Examples: marble (from limestone), slate (from shale), gneiss (from granite).

qa.q: Can one type of rock become another type? Explain with the diagram.
qa.a: Yes. Igneous rocks are weathered into sediments that form sedimentary rocks. Heat and pressure change rocks into metamorphic rocks, which can melt into magma.

sum.title: III. The Rock Cycle
items: Illustration
Copy the rock cycle: rocks slowly change from one type to another over millions of years.
rock_cycle.png

evaluation: A rock is a natural, solid material of the crust made of one or more minerals.
Give one example each of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.
Why does sandstone often show layers?
It is a sedimentary rock, made of layers of sand deposited one after another.
remediation: Rocks formed from cooled magma are ______ rocks.
Rocks formed from layers of sediments are ______ rocks.
Rocks changed by heat and pressure are ______ rocks.
Fossils are found mainly in ______ rocks.
The change of rocks from one type to another is the rock ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. igneous 2. sedimentary 3. metamorphic 4. limestone 5. sedimentary 6. cycle
end.homework: Look at a map of the world. Cut out, or trace, Africa and South America and try to fit their coasts together. Write what you notice.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 9: The Theory of Continental Drift.
teacherNote: Correction: the source situation used mud bricks as an example of sedimentary rock. Mud bricks are made by people. The situation now uses sandstone blocks.
Correction: "Sedimentary rocks are the only rocks that contain fossils" is too strong. Fossils are found mainly in sedimentary rocks.
Local examples checked: limestone of Figuil (cement), Cretaceous sandstones of the Benue basin around Garoua, granite of the Mandara Mountains, basalt of Mount Cameroon.
